application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client library built on the fetch API, providing automatic JSON handling, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized errors for Node.js and browser environments.
application.purpose: Simplify making HTTP requests and handling responses, errors, and retries in JavaScript/TypeScript applications.

domains.name: HTTP Client
domains.description: Core request construction, sending, and response parsing over fetch.

domains.name: Error Handling
domains.description: Normalizes failed requests and responses into structured FetchError objects with status and request details.

domains.name: Retry and Timeout
domains.description: Automatic retries for transient failures and request timeouts via abort signals.

domains.name: Request Preparation
domains.description: Merges default and per-request options, headers, query parameters, and serializes JSON bodies.

domains.name: Runtime Adaptation
domains.description: Selects fetch, Headers, and AbortController implementations for global, Node.js, and polyfilled environments.

applicationFacts: The deterministic graph contains 12 function entities and 10 CALLS relations, all originating within createFetch or its helper chain.
createFetch is the central orchestrator and calls resolveFetchOptions, callHooks, isPayloadMethod, isJSONSerializable, onError, and detectResponseType.
onError calls isPayloadMethod and createFetchError and may recursively re-invoke $fetchRaw for retries.
Retry defaults differ: payload methods default to 0 retries while other methods default to 1 unless configured.
Response bodies are parsed with destr for JSON by default, or via a custom parseResponse function.
src/index.ts exports a browser-oriented ofetch and $fetch using global fetch; src/node.ts provides a Node.js variant with optional keep-alive agents.
Build config defines two entry points, src/index and src/node, and marks undici as external.
Timeouts are implemented by aborting the request with a TimeoutError after the configured duration.
unknowns: The graph does not include entities for types, constants, or exported class methods, so their roles are described only from source.
CALLS relations for calls to external libraries (destr, ufo, node-fetch-native) are not present in the graph and are not modeled.

The CALLS relation from createFetch to itself and the call to $fetchRaw from onError are present in the source but the graph does not expose $fetchRaw as an entity, so the recursive retry path is not represented as a distinct node.
The intended consumers and deployment context beyond the README-level purpose are not stated in the provided source.
Whether test/index.test.ts#abortHandle is an isolated test function or is invoked as part of a test case is not determinable from the graph alone.
